Fine motor:
An informal fine motor screen was administered to assess xx overall fine motor skills.

* Pencil grasp and bilateral coordination– She uses a dynamic tripod grasp when writing. She rested her helper hand in her lap at first, but held the paper steady after a verbal cue..
* Coloring – She colored a 2-inch star and stayed within the border on all but one point.
* Cutting – During cutting tasks, she opened and closed the scissors with a smooth rhythm and turned the paper with her helper hand. She cut a complex shape (heart) with two small deviations.
* Tool Use – She was able to functionally use fine motor tools including a glue stick and tape.
* Handwriting Sample – When given a two-sentence (14 words) sample to copy, she spaced her words evenly, used lowercase letters where expected, and kept letters on the baseline for 80% of words. However, her letters drifted larger toward the end of each line, she skipped the word "to," and she misspelled one word ("jmup" for "jump"). However, her overall writing is within normal age expectations. Her classroom writing sample showed the same drift in size and a tendency to crowd the right margin. When asked to recall the alphabet from memory without cues, she recalled 24/26 uppercase and lowercase letters, demonstrating reversals on J and S. When provided with cues during letter copying, she demonstrated the motor skills to copy all uppercase and lowercase letters without letter reversals or incorrect formation, suggesting functional motor skills. Overall, her writing was generally legible, though primarily impacted by letter size, suggesting she may benefit from paper with a highlighted writing zone, as well as a visual reminder to leave a margin.

Sensory Processing:
Sensory Integration is the process by which information from our senses (touch, taste, smell, sight, hearing and balance/movement) is interpreted by the brain so the body can respond to the environment.  Sensory responses may also affect a person's ability to adequately engage in the environment as well as affect emotions and behaviors.
During clinical observations, XX demonstrated difficulty with sustained attention, often leaving his chair to look out of the window and humming while he worked, which impacted his ability to sustain attention during testing.
The Sensory Processing Measure- 2: School form was completed by XX’s teacher to help determine areas of sensory processing that are impacting XX within the classroom.  Subtests include:  Social Participation, Vision, Hearing, Touch, Taste and Smell, Body Awareness, Balance and Motion, Planning and Ideas.  In each area, a child can fall under either Typical, Moderate Difficulties, or Severe Difficulties.  XX results are as follows:
Typical Processing:

* Taste and Smell
* Vision

Moderate Difficulties:

* Social Participation
* Touch

Severe Difficulties:

* Hearing
* Body awareness
* Balance and Motion
* Planning and ideas
* Sensory total

Teacher rating form
Based on the Teacher Rating Form completed by the special education teacher, XX demonstrates fine motor delays 51–79% of the time, which interfere with his independence and access to the general education  curriculum. Identified areas of concern include letter sizing, line adherence, coloring, cutting, buttoning, and opening containers.  Additionally, handwriting mechanics such as legibility, letter formation, line anchoring, and spacing are challenging.  His sensory behaviors are also of concern specifically a habit of chewing on his sleeves and covering his ears during assemblies interfere with his functioning in the classroom setting. To support his overall performance and attention, effective classroom accommodations currently in use include a chewable pencil topper, a seat near the door, and a visual schedule.

Impact of Disability Statement

XX [XX disability]] impacts his fine motor skills, self-help skills, and sensory processing skills in the classroom. His fine motor deficits impact his ability to show what he knows through written work. These fine motor and self-care limitations slow his transitions between activities and his set-up for lunch, which shortens his instructional time. His sensory processing skills affect his attention when participating within the classroom environment, as he covers his ears during loud activities and leaves his seat to seek movement. He would benefit from occupational therapy services to address fine motor, visual-motor, self-help, and sensory-motor skill development to facilitate his ability to access the educational environment.  These impacts limit his timely completion of classwork and full participation in age-appropriate classroom tasks.

Service delivery statement

Occupational Therapy services will be provided by a licensed Registered Occupational Therapist or by a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant under the supervision of a Registered Occupational Therapist. XX minutes of occupational therapy will be provided outside the classroom to address fine motor and visual motor integration skills, sensory processing and self help skills.  Services may be 1:1 or within a small group.

Physical Motor Goal
By March of 2028, after given direct instruction in Fine Motor skill development, XX  will meet the following 2 out of 3 objectives on 80% of opportunities OR over 3 out of 4 data collection dates:
XX will improve fine motor cutting skills needed to manage classroom paper tasks by accurately cutting along a curved line within 1/4 inch of the boundary line.
XX will fasten the top button of his coat and engage the zipper pin, given a visual sequence card and no more than one verbal cue.
XX will improve visual motor skills needed to access written work by legibly copying letters and shapes with slanted lines (i.e. triangle, X, R, K, Q, Y, y).
Related Standards

1. WLP.1.1. Independently print legible letters, numerals, and punctuation on grade-level appropriate lined paper.
2. Fine motor skills: F2.2 Apply movement concepts to specific movement situations. Uses crayons, markers, pencils independently; uses a dough/clay tools; uses scissors
3. Standards Based Life Skill Curriculum Intermediate: Undress and dress self, including buttons and fasteners
